name: 1MCP Agent

hlido_opinion.headline: A well-argued fix for MCP context sprawl — progressive tool discovery so agents stop carrying the whole tool catalogue in context. Still beta, and honest about it.
hlido_opinion.body: 1MCP Agent aggregates MCP servers behind a single runtime (`1mcp serve`) and then does the more interesting thing: instead of injecting every tool schema into an agent's context, it offers a CLI mode where the agent starts with `instructions`, narrows with `inspect`, and only runs the tool it actually needs. The problem statement is stated crisply and is real — configuration sprawl across clients, and context sprawl inside long-running agent loops — and progressive discovery is a genuine architectural answer rather than a repackaging. The documentation is the strong point: a five-minute setup path with copy-pasteable commands, explicit guidance on which path to choose (CLI mode, proxy, or direct streamable HTTP) and why, and per-client setup for Codex, Claude and Cursor. Presets, filters, template-backed servers, and async/lazy loading round it out. The main caution is maturity: the captured version is v0.35.0-beta.3, a pre-1.0 beta, and the surface offers no adoption numbers, named users, or third-party validation. Nothing here is overclaimed — the docs are careful about what each path is for — but a runtime that sits between every agent and every tool is exactly the component where beta status matters.

tier_rationale: STEADY (74) for a real, well-diagnosed problem (MCP config and context sprawl), a genuine architectural answer (progressive discovery: instructions → inspect → run), and documentation good enough to get a working setup in five minutes with explicit path guidance. Held well below VITAL because the captured release is v0.35.0-beta.3 — pre-1.0 — with no adoption evidence or third-party validation, and this is precisely the kind of always-in-the-path component where beta maturity carries weight.
what_it_does_well: Diagnoses two distinct real problems — client configuration sprawl and agent context sprawl — and addresses both
Progressive discovery (instructions → inspect → run) genuinely reduces what an agent must hold in context
Documentation gives an explicit five-minute path with runnable commands and per-client setup (Codex, Claude, Cursor)
Clear guidance on choosing between CLI mode, proxy, and direct streamable HTTP, with the trade-off stated for each
Presets and filters let server sets be reused across projects and clients without duplicating config
Async and lazy loading — starts faster and exposes less until something actually needs it
what_it_fails_at: Captured release is v0.35.0-beta.3 — pre-1.0 beta, in a component that sits in the path of every tool call
No adoption numbers, named users, or third-party validation on the public surface
No stated reliability, performance, or overhead figures for the aggregation layer
Adds an operational dependency: if the runtime is down, every aggregated server is unreachable
Not tested hands-on — the context-reduction claim is the one that most needs measuring
best_for: Developers running several MCP servers across multiple AI clients who are tired of duplicating configuration
Long-running agent loops where injected tool schemas are consuming meaningful context
Teams wanting one place to manage server sets, presets and filters
not_recommended_for: Production deployments that require a stable 1.0 with a support commitment
Setups with a single MCP server, where the aggregation layer adds cost and no benefit
Anyone who cannot accept a new single point of failure between agents and tools

evidence_urls.claim: Unified MCP runtime via `1mcp serve` aggregating static and template-backed servers
Progressive CLI discovery: instructions → inspect → run
Published as @1mcp/agent on npm with a five-minute setup path

agent_relevance.agent_integration_path: Built entirely for agent consumption: `1mcp serve` is the runtime, CLI mode is the agent-facing workflow, and proxy plus direct streamable HTTP cover MCP-native clients. Agents are the only intended user.

checklist.evidence: 'One runtime for MCP, one thinner workflow for agents'
Open npm package; no pricing surface (appears free/open)
Documentation and command examples only — no benchmarks or adoption evidence
